_why: The household words for a room this site names differently. Every entry is measured, not guessed: the 'queries' and 'covered' figures are from ops/keyword-demand.json's 2026-10-02 harvest, which ran the VOCABULARY_PROBES seeds added to ops/keyword_demand.py for exactly this question. A word earns a place here only if people type it AND this site does not already answer for it.
_rule: Do not add a word with no measured queries. 'master closet', 'rec room', 'ensuite' and 'lounge' were all considered and all returned zero, so naming them would be inventing demand. Do not add a word the site already covers: 'linen closet' (51 queries, 24 covered), 'coat closet' (21, 11), 'walk in closet' (34, 15) and 'front hall' (6, 4) are all answered already and adding them would be noise. 'utility room' was wrongly kept on this list until 2026-10-31: its 'covered' queries scored against /articles/how-to-organize-a-basement.html, matched only because that page's own unrelated headings happen to carry both words ('3. The utility zone: keep it clear' and '6. The room you actually use'), not because the Laundry Room, the real answer, said anything about being a utility room at all. See the Laundry Room entry below.

Kids Bedroom.source: Found 2026-11-06, scheduled operator cycle, mining Primary Bedroom's partial tier (ops/room_guide_underperformance.py --room 'Primary Bedroom'): 'boys bedroom organization ideas', 'how to organize a boys bedroom', 'how to organise a boys bedroom', 'childrens bedroom organization ideas', 'how to organise a girls bedroom', 'how to declutter children's bedroom' and 'how to organize a small children's bedroom' (7 unique queries, 10 rows across both harvests) all scored partial against /articles/how-to-declutter-a-bedroom.html (Primary Bedroom's own guide), unmatched only on the child word each time. This is the exact A25/A26 Guest-vs-Primary tie-break shape, not a new bug: the purpose-built page for this already exists and already answers the identical plain phrasing perfectly ('kids bedroom organization ideas' and six siblings score covered at /articles/how-to-organize-a-kids-bedroom.html, grep-confirmed, zero relation invented here), but with no room signal for 'boys'/'girls'/'childrens'/children's', the exact-score tie (both pages match on the bare word 'bedroom' alone) falls to url order, and 'declutter' sorts before 'organize'. Checked the losing page honestly before naming this a misroute, not assumed: how-to-declutter-a-bedroom.html does carry a real, relevant section ('A very messy room, or a child's room') that answers the general decluttering process for a child's room, so routing a plain 'child's bedroom' singular query there (already covered, left alone) is not wrong. The four names added here are specifically the ones a parent of a boy, a girl, or children (plural) types, which is Kids Bedroom's own already-published subject, not this article's. 'kids bedroom design ideas for girls' was checked and correctly excluded: the substring 'girls bedroom' does not appear in it ('ideas for girls', different word order), and that query already scores partial at the correct kids-bedroom page, a different, smaller gap (unmatched 'design'/'girls') left for a future cycle. Verified against the real household_room_signal()/_tie_break() mechanism in ops/keyword_demand.py (A26) before adding, not assumed: both candidate pages are curated ROOM_GUIDES entries, so room_of() via guide_article_rooms() already tags them Primary Bedroom and Kids Bedroom respectively, and _tie_break() prefers the page matching a detected room signal on an exact score tie, which this is.

Home Office.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-11-01 (ca): 'home office organization tips for creating a productive workspace', rank 12, gap, 0.333 coverage, scored to /home-office-deck.html. 'Workspace' is the plain household word for this room; the page carried no 'workspace' wording anywhere (grep-confirmed) before this entry. 'Creating', 'productive' and 'tips' stay unmatched: generic listicle filler, not facts this product states about the room, the same discipline 'plan'/'design' were held to in the Room layout tips.

Entryway.source_hallway: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-11-05, ops/keyword-demand.json: 29 queries containing 'hallway' across both harvests, most already covered against Hall Closet's own longer 'hallway closet' synonym (which wins the room-signal tie by length per household_room_signal's longest-match rule, so no collision). Four remain partial with the bare word 'hallway' unmatched: 'hallway coat closet organization ideas' (content words hallway/coat/closet, already carrying 'coat'+'closet' from the entryway article, only 'hallway' missing), 'how to declutter hallway', 'how to decorate a small entrance hallway' (already carries the 'entrance hall' room signal, 'small' stays a separate cross-room modifier), and 'hallway cabinet organization ideas' (checked and left alone: a hallway storage cabinet is a genuine word-sense ambiguity with nothing this site answers, not improved by this entry). Grep-confirmed before this edit: no page's title or h1-h3 headings carried 'hallway' except Hall Closet's own pages, so this is not already covered elsewhere and cannot collide with them (the Hall Closet synonym 'hallway closet' is a longer string and always wins the household_room_signal tie-break when both appear).

Hall Closet.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-10-23 (gb, au, in) for 'hall cupboard'. 'hallway closet' added 2026-11-04, scheduled operator cycle: 'how to organize a deep hallway closet' and 'how to organize a small hallway closet' (both tiers) plus 'small hallway closet organization ideas' (global) all score 'partial' (0.667) against an unrelated page (how-to-organize-a-linen-closet.html or how-to-organize-a-laundry-room.html) via a tied word-overlap collision on 'organize'/'closet' alone, the same alphabetical-tie-break shape A25/A26/A37 already named, because no Hall Closet page carries the word 'hallway' anywhere in a heading. Most 'hallway closet' queries already score 'covered' against hall-closet-deck.html, which does carry 'hallway' (card headings about a hallway chair and a toddler loose in the hallway) and 'closet', confirming this is the real room; the three partial rows differ only in using 'deep'/'small', which do not change the real destination. The room's own intro ('the hall closet is the darkest and deepest storage in the house') and name already describe exactly this closet in the hallway, so 'hallway closet' is the plain household name for it, not an invented one. 'under stairs cupboard' added 2026-11-05, scheduled operator cycle, continuing entry 131's handoff to mine the 'stairs' cluster the global harvest's partial rows surfaced: 'how to organise under stairs cupboard' (gb), 'how to organise under stairs storage' (gb) and 'how to organize closet under stairs' (gb, au, ca, in) all score 'partial' with only the bare word 'stairs' unmatched, against wrong pages (a kitchen cabinet zone, a generic downloads page) because no page anywhere names this space. The British/Commonwealth cupboard under the stairs is the same real storage space this room's own intro already describes ('the darkest and deepest storage in the house'), the household catch-all closet for vacuum, cleaning supplies and seasonal gear, not a separate room; checked against content.json before adding (Cleaning Equipment Zone, Cleaning Supply Zone and Seasonal and Guest Zone all match what this space actually holds). Named 'under stairs cupboard' rather than the more natural 'understairs cupboard' or 'cupboard under the stairs' for two reasons found in sequence, both checked directly rather than assumed: the compound 'understairs cupboard' rebuilt clean but moved zero rows on rescore, because the scorer's word() tokenizer treats 'understairs' as one token, not a match for the query token 'stairs' (the same literal-word-not-stem bar A34/A36 already learned for nappy/nappies and craft/crafts); 'cupboard under the stairs' then failed test_room_also_called.py's own evidence check, because that exact phrase appears in zero harvested queries, only reordered variants do. 'under stairs cupboard' is the literal substring of the real harvested query 'how to organise under stairs cupboard', satisfying both the evidence test and the tokenizer. Re-rescored and confirmed moved before shipping. Grep-confirmed before this edit: no page's title or h1-h3 headings anywhere on the site carried 'stairs' except Stair Landing's own pages, which are about the landing surface and floor path, not storage, so no content-based collision.

Laundry Room.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-10-31 (gb, au, ca, in). All 26 global queries plus 15 more in the US harvest (ops/keyword-demand.json) were scoring 'covered' or 'partial' against /articles/how-to-organize-a-basement.html or /articles/how-long-does-it-take-to-organise-a-room.html, neither of which is about this room; 'covered' is recorded as 0 here because none of that was earned by a Laundry Room page, which carried no 'utility room' wording at all until this entry.

Patio or Deck.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-10-29 (in) for 'terrace'; 2026-10-31 (au) for 'backyard'; 2026-11-01 (gb) for 'porch'. 'backyard organisation' (rank 7, au) scored 'gap' against /about.html on a coincidental title match, not because that page is about this room; the Patio or Deck page's own six zones (seating, grilling, dining, garden, storage, the surface/rail/safety zone) are exactly what a household means by 'backyard', and the page carried no 'backyard' wording at all until this entry. 'porch organisation' (rank 10, gb) scored 'gap' against /about.html the same way; 'porch' is the plain British/Commonwealth word for the same outdoor seating structure this room already covers, confirmed by grep: neither the room page nor the deck page carried the word at all before this entry. Thin evidence (one query each) but real, not invented.

Mudroom.source: ops/keyword-demand.json 2026-11-05, ops/room_guide_underperformance.py --room Mudroom: 'how to organize mudroom lockers' (partial, 0.5 title coverage) and 'mudroom locker organization ideas' (partial, 0.5 title coverage), both already scored to this room's own pages (mudroom-deck.html or a zone page) via the word 'mudroom', only 'lockers'/'locker' unmatched. Neither word appeared anywhere in this site's titles or h1-h3 headings before this entry (grep-confirmed, including the sample-chapters download, where 'locker' appears once in body prose about a rented storage locker, not a heading). A built-in mudroom locker system, assigned hooks plus a cubby or bench per person, is exactly what the Family Hook Zone and Bench and Transition Surface already describe; it names the whole room's built-in system, not one specific zone, the same shape as 'porch'/'terrace' above, so it belongs at room level. Both the plural and singular forms are added because the scorer does no stemming (confirmed in ops/keyword_demand.py's own _morphology_variants docstring: it is used only for tie-break near-miss credit, never the primary score), and each form matches a different real query. Thin evidence (one query per form) but real, not invented.

_global_note: Entries carrying a 'source' were measured by ops/keyword_demand_global.py, which harvests the same seeds for gb, au, ca and in. ops/tests/test_room_also_called.py accepts evidence from either harvest.
